Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This reduction(max : maxError, relError)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random Every GPU (one OpenMP thread per local GPU) updates its row blocks below\n//      the diagonal block with a tiled GEMM (prefix sum over k < j0) and a\n//      short in-block fix-up kernel.\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr size_t BS = 64;  // row block height and panel width\nconstexpr int TM = 16;     // output rows per CTA of the prefix GEMM\nconstexpr int TN = 16;     // output columns per CTA (BS / TN column tiles)\nconstexpr int TK = 32;     // k-tile depth of the prefix GEMM\n\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Sum over k < j0 of L[i][k] * P[c][k] for a range of rows and the panel columns\n// c < w. Grid: (row tiles, BS / TN column tiles).\n// L rows are addressed as L[(lrStart + r) * n + k]; S receives BS entries per row.\n__global__ void gemmPrefixKernel(const double* __restrict__ L, const double* __restrict__ P,\n                                 double* __restrict__ S, size_t lrStart, size_t nRows,\n                                 int w, size_t j0, size_t n) {\n    __shared__ double sA[TM][TK + 1];\n    __shared__ double sB[TN][TK + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int tid = ty * TN + tx;\n    const size_t rowBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * TM;\n    const int colBase = blockIdx.y * TN;\n\n    double acc = 0.0;\n    for (size_t kt = 0; kt < j0; kt += TK) {\n        for (int idx = tid; idx < TM * TK; idx += TM * TN) {\n            const int r = idx / TK;\n            const int kk = idx % TK;\n            const size_t rr = rowBase + r;\n            const size_t k = kt + kk;\n            sA[r][kk] = (rr < nRows && k < j0) ? Columns are processed sequentially, rows in parallel.\n__global__ void diagBlockKernel(double* __restrict__ L, const double* __restrict__ S,\n                                size_t lrT, size_t j0, int w, size_t n, int* fail) {\n    __shared__ double sL[BS][BS];\n    __shared__ double sD[BS];\n\n    const int r = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t lr = lrT + r;\n\n    for (int c = 0; idx < w * w; idx += blockDim.x) {\n        const int c = idx / w;\n        const int cc = idx % w;\n        sP[c][cc] = P[c * n + j0 + cc];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (r < nRows) {\n        double* row = L + (lrStart + r) * n + j0;\n        const double* srow = S + (lrStart + r) * BS;\n        for (int c = 0; The executable is still `cholesky`, and no files were added to the project. It's about 110× faster than the original at n=4096, and it passes validation for every rank count I tested.\n\n**Design**\n- **CUDA:** the row blocks (64 rows each) are spread block-cyclically over all GPUs, one worker per GPU. Each block column is handled in three steps. The owner GPU factors the diagonal block, the panel is broadcast, and every GPU updates its own rows with a tiled GEMM plus a short in-block fix-up kernel. No cuBLAS or other library is used, so there are no new dependencies.\n- **MPI:** each rank drives the GPUs on its node, and the panel is broadcast with `MPI_Bcast`. Rank 0 gathers L for output and validation. Failure is broadcast so all ranks exit together.\n- **OpenMP:** used for matrix generation, the validation loops, and the per-step loop over local GPUs.\n- **Semantics:** each element's dot product is still accumulated in ascending k order into one accumulator, so the results don't depend on rank or GPU count. Output format, the `-n/-v/-r/-h` options, the non-positive-definite message and the timing line are unchanged.\n- **Build:** CMake requires CUDA, MPI and OpenMP, with no fallback path. CUDA architectures default to 70/80/86/90, overridable with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`. Sum, Min, Max and the samples agree with the original to 1e-9 relative.\n- The hash differs from the original for n > 1. I traced one element to FMA contraction. The original's compiler fuses some of the dot-product steps and not others, depending on code shape, so the original's own rounding can't be copied exactly on the GPU. Keeping FMA on was faster and gave a smaller error than turning it off. No cuBLAS or other library is used, so there are no new dependencies.\n- **MPI:** each rank drives the GPUs on its node, and the panel is broadcast with `MPI_Bcast`. Rank 0 gathers L for output and validation. Failure is broadcast so all ranks exit together.\n- **OpenMP:** used for matrix generation, the validation loops, and the per-step loop over local GPUs.\n- **Semantics:** each element's dot product is still accumulated in ascending k order into one accumulator, so the results don't depend on rank or GPU count. Output format, the `-n/-v/-r/-h` options, the non-positive-definite message and the timing line are unchanged.\n- **Build:** CMake requires CUDA, MPI and OpenMP, with no fallback path. CUDA architectures default to 70/80/86/90, overridable with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`. The `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA because the kernels live in it.\n\n**Verification**\n- Against the original's output for n = 1, 7, 64, 65, 333, 512, 1000 with 1, 2, 4 and 8 ranks, all 28 runs pass validation. Sum, Min, Max and the samples agree with the original to 1e-9 relative.\n- The hash differs from the original for n > 1. I traced one element to FMA contraction. The original's compiler fuses some of the dot-product steps and not others, depending on code shape, so the original's own rounding can't be copied exactly on the GPU. Keeping FMA on was faster and gave a smaller error than turning it off. This is a last-bit difference, not an algorithmic one, but it means `-r` output won't hash-match the original.\n- The non-positive-definite path was checked with a debug copy in `/tmp`, since the real generator always produces a valid matrix. It reports the correct index and both ranks exit with status 1.\n\n**Performance** (4× RTX 3090)\n\n| n | Original | Hybrid, 1 rank | Hybrid, 2 ranks | Hybrid, 4 ranks |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 2048 | 2144 ms | 54 ms | 49 ms | 70 ms |\n| 4096 | 17.9 s | 161 ms | 161 ms | 131 ms |\n\nThese are single-node numbers only, and I didn't test multi-node. Running 8 ranks on 4 GPUs was slower (314 ms).\n\n**Choices to review**\n- The timer starts after device setup and allocation, the way the matrix allocation sits outside the original's timer. It includes the host→device upload and the factorization, and excludes the gather and validation.\n- Each rank keeps a full host copy of A, so host memory is n² per rank. The per-step broadcast isn't overlapped with compute.\n\n**Issues found and fixed along the way**\n- CMake's `native` architecture detection fell back to sm_52. The defaults are now set before `project()`, which was where the fallback came from.\n- Open MPI's C++ bindings were producing warnings, so `OMPI_SKIP_MPICXX` is defined.","ttft_ms":821,"type":"result","duration_ms":2179702,"uuid":"9416f1db-f957-440d-86da-b11150d23227","ttft_stream_ms":738,"time_to_request_ms":149,"first_content_frame_ms":738,"queued_turn_count":0,"result_index":0}
